invariants.statement: The positive conformance corpus forms an end-to-end digest-linked signed artifact graph; unresolved or substituted internal references are prohibited.
Each one-shot Permit in the positive corpus resolves to one exact signed CoreResolution that binds the exact Submission and Permit digest.
ASET-JCS-1 canonical bytes, SHA-256 digests and Ed25519 signatures are verified against reproducible positive and negative vectors.
Signed normative JSON values prohibit non-integer numbers unless a future version defines and tests a complete cross-language numeric canonicalization profile.
ASET-JCS-1 permits only I-JSON safe integers and sorts NFC-normalized object keys by unsigned UTF-8 bytes using published cross-language edge vectors.
Every stable ID in the normative machine model is globally unique; conflicting duplicate identities are prohibited.
Every primary identity in requirements, ADR, verification, model, diagram, conformance, oracle, document and key registries is unique in its declared registry.
Every normative JSON input rejects duplicate raw member names before semantic parsing, schema validation, digesting or signature verification.
Every normative JSON artifact is validated by a closed-world schema with unknown properties rejected.
All 11 gates have distinct submission, Permit and patch schemas; a document valid for one role is invalid for every incompatible role.
The externally signed freeze profile binds the path, schema $id, byte SHA-256 and canonical digest of every mandatory normative JSON Schema before any schema is used.
Protocol validation and canonicalization contain no module business logic and issue no Permit.
